Camino Health Center

Dashed amber ring = lease expiring within 24 months. Click a Camino pin for its market position.

Hospitals & Health Systems

Every Hoag, MemorialCare and Providence site from the Orange County Medical Community report — hospitals plus outpatient clinics, imaging, cancer, rehab and pharmacy locations. Popups carry the category and whether the site is Owned or Leased. Larger dots are acute-care hospitals.

Health Centers (FQHC + HRSA)

FQHC (Federally Qualified Health Center) and HRSA (Health Resources & Services Administration) lists merged with duplicates removed — one pin per site. Blue = FQHC-designated, green = HRSA-listed only. Default shows the standalone clinic sites; the sub-toggle adds school-based clinics, mobile units/trailers and shelter sites. Camino's own clinics are on the Camino layer. The 1-mile rings are always drawn on the 51 FQHC-designated sites and come and go with this layer.

Rural Health Clinic Path

A Rural Health Clinic is a separate Medicare certification from Federally Qualified Health Center status — not a waiver of it. It carries its own cost-based reimbursement, and the two cannot be held by the same site at the same time. A clinic has to meet all three of the following.

Where it sits. In an area the Census does not classify as urbanized, that also carries a current shortage designation — a Health Professional Shortage Area, a Medically Underserved Area, or a shortage area designated by the Governor — awarded within the last four years.

How it is staffed. Under the medical direction of a physician, employing at least one nurse practitioner or physician assistant, with a nurse practitioner, physician assistant or certified nurse-midwife on site providing patient care for at least half the hours the clinic is open.

What it cannot be. A rehabilitation agency, or a facility mainly treating mental illness. And one site cannot be certified as both a Rural Health Clinic and a Federally Qualified Health Center at once.

What that means here. Camino’s five locations all sit in urbanized south Orange County, so this route does not apply to the existing clinics. It is a path for a prospective new site in a qualifying rural tract, which is what the rural census layer is for.

Criteria summarised from CMS Rural Health Clinic guidance (42 CFR 491) and the Rural Health Information Hub. Shortage-area designations change, so confirm current status with CMS and HRSA before relying on this for a site decision.

Medical Availabilities (CoStar)

Every building with a 3,000–6,000 SF contiguous space available. Tick South of SR-55 only to narrow to Camino's south county market — everything south and east of SR-55 (State Route 55, the Costa Mesa Freeway) — and the shading follows it. Tick Hide availabilities within 1 mile of an FQHC to surface only locations that are not already served. Source: CoStar export 9/3/2026 · Orange County only.

Riverside County Market

Every Riverside County building with a 3,000–6,000 sq ft contiguous medical space available. Buildings group into three markets: Riverside and Corona, the Temecula–Murrieta corridor, and the desert cities from Palm Springs out to Indio. Hollow dots are the two buildings opening in 2027 that are not built yet. Source: CoStar export 9/8/2026 · Riverside County only. All 53 are on the map; the two Highway 111 addresses were positioned by hand because no geocoder would resolve them.
